scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on the CS LAB 1 PC (192.168.2.3) reports they cannot reach
the Server Room (1.0.0.x) or the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x). The
IT Department PCs are also affected. Other zones (Office, Principle,
Internet Lab itself) can still reach each other. What's wrong?
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router0 ripd daemon
Mechanism: router0 is the only L3 hop between IT Dept
  (192.168.1.0/24), CS Dept (192.168.2.0/24), and the rest
  of the network (reached via Serial2/0 to router1). When
  ripd dies on router0, router1 ages out the 192.168.1.0/24
  and 192.168.2.0/24 prefixes, and router0 itself stops
  learning the 1.0.0.0/8 / 128.168.0.0/16 / 192.168.3.0/24
  / 192.168.4.0/24 prefixes from router1. IT + CS PCs become
  isolated from everything beyond router0.
Localization: router0
Root cause: RIP routing daemon (ripd) not running on router0
Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration on router0 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ripd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router rip` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ripd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the rip configuration is missing/empty on router0" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ripd daemon on router0 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
router0). Once ripd is running again it re-learns the remote prefixes and
re-advertises 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, restoring IT Dept and CS Dept
reachability.

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ripd back CONFIG-LESS and the rip service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ripd AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration (network statements) on router0. A proposal that restores the missing rip configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The RIP routing daemon (ripd) has been killed and is completely absent on
router0, and its configuration file (/etc/frr/frr.conf) does not exist.
The FRR service itself is marked inactive (dead). Only the ancillary zebra,
mgmtd, and staticd processes are still running.

Without ripd, router0 cannot participate in RIP and therefore learns no
routes beyond its three directly connected networks (192.168.1.0/24 –
IT Dept, 192.168.2.0/24 – CS LAB, 10.10.0.1/8 – WAN to router1). It has
no entries for the Server Room (1.0.0.0/8) or Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16),
which are reachable only through router1 → router2. Any packet from a CS or
IT host destined for those networks arrives at router0's gateway (192.168.2.1
or 192.168.1.1) and is silently dropped — confirmed by 100% packet loss from
cs_lab1 to both 1.0.0.1 and 128.168.0.2.

Router1 and router2 are healthy: router1 still has stale RIP entries for
router0's subnets (timer ≈2 min until expiry), and router2 has full visibility
of the rest of the topology. The Office and Principle subnets are unaffected
because they use router1 as their gateway, which has a complete RIP table.

Root cause: the ripd daemon was stopped/killed on router0 and the FRR
configuration file was removed, leaving router0 with no dynamic routing.

Corrective fix: restore a valid /etc/frr/frr.conf on router0 containing the
RIP router block with network statements covering 10.0.0.0/8 (WAN),
192.168.1.0/24 (IT), and 192.168.2.0/24 (CS), then restart the FRR service
(service frr restart) to bring ripd back up. Routes will converge within one
RIP update cycle (≤30 s).

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names router0 as the affected device multiple times (e.g., ripd killed on router0, configuration missing on router0).
The agent explicitly identifies the RIP routing daemon (ripd) on router0 as the failed component and attributes the outage to ripd/RIP being stopped.
Agent explicitly identifies that IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24) hosts are isolated while other subnets (Office, Principle) remain unaffected.
The agent recommends restoring the RIP configuration (network statements) and restarting the FRR/ripd service, which matches the expected remediation.

The agent's investigation shows direct observations (ripd absent, empty/absent FRR config, limited routing table on router0, running zebra/mgmtd, and host ping failures) and draws logical inferences linking ripd being dead/missing config to loss of RIP routes and host isolation. The checks performed and the recommended fix match the ground-truth fault and remediation.
